scope: ERA5 reanalysis surface meteorology over Hong Kong from 2024-12, sampled on the ERA5 grid itself. Produced by scripts/ingest/fetch_era5.py --domain HK. Added for one quantity the territory has no other source for: boundary-layer height at every hour. The radiosondes measure the vertical structure directly but only at 08:00 and 20:00, which brackets the daytime mixed layer without ever sampling it.

files.met_era5.csv: One row per grid cell per hour: boundary-layer height, 10 m wind speed and direction, 2 m temperature, surface pressure, ventilation coefficient.

sources.title: ERA5 hourly data on single levels from 1940 to present
sources.notes: product_type=reanalysis, area [22.6, 113.8, 22.1, 114.5]. Requested variables: boundary_layer_height, 10m_u_component_of_wind, 10m_v_component_of_wind, 2m_temperature, surface_pressure. Native resolution 0.25 degrees, hourly.

sampling.why_grid_cells_not_stations: Beijing's ERA5 tables are sampled at its twelve monitoring stations. Hong Kong's station coordinates live in a database this ingest cannot open, and taking them from a public source instead would repeat the provenance hazard that `beijing_station_coordinate_audit` exists to document. Sampling on ERA5's own grid needs no external coordinates at all.
sampling.kings_park_cell: grid_22.25N_114.25E — the cell containing 22.3119N, 114.1728E, so this is the one that pairs with the soundings and the radiation records.
sampling.why_all_six_are_kept: They disagree. At a given hour the boundary-layer height spreads a median of 177 m across the six, a 95th percentile of 563 m and a maximum of 1,576 m — the southern cells sit over water and the northern ones against the mainland. Annual means are nearly identical (445 to 500 m), so this is an hour-scale signal rather than a bias, and averaging or picking one cell would discard it.

conventions.time: Hong Kong local standard time (UTC+8). ERA5 stamps in UTC; the ingest shifts it, and pulls a boundary pad from the preceding month so the first local day of each month is not short by eight hours.
conventions.station_column: `station` holds grid-cell names, not monitoring sites. The column is named `station` only to match the shape of the Beijing tables.
conventions.wind_direction: The direction the wind blows FROM, per meteorological convention.
conventions.ventilation: blh_m x wind_speed_ms, with the factors rounded first so the product is reproducible from the published columns. About 0.4 % of rows still disagree by exactly 0.1 when recomputed — the product lands on a .x5 boundary that the CSV round trip resolves the other way. A case asking for this quantity needs a tolerance of at least 0.1.

verification.completeness: 87,984 rows over the full days 2024-12-01 to 2026-08-03: exactly 144 rows per day (6 cells x 24 h) on every day, no missing values in any field.
verification.diurnal_cycle: Median boundary-layer height at the King's Park cell runs from 362 m at 19:00 to 642 m at 14:00 — deepest in the afternoon, collapsing after sunset, which is the expected shape in local time.
verification.physical_ranges: blh 10.7 to 2,098 m; wind 0 to 30.8 m/s; temperature 8.6 to 35.1 C; pressure 975.3 to 1,030.8 hPa. Nothing out of range.
verification.spatial_spread: Median 177 m between the six cells at a given hour, 95th percentile 563 m, maximum 1,576 m.

coverage.note: The two partial days are the boundary pad at the start and the end of the download window. Exclude them from daily or monthly statistics.

known_limits: This is MODEL output, not measurement. A case must say 'ERA5-estimated boundary-layer height' rather than 'observed'; the radiosondes in profile_sounding.csv are the observational counterpart, at two hours a day.

Grid-cell choice changes the answer. With up to 1,576 m between cells at the same hour, any question about boundary-layer height has to name its cell or its aggregation rule, or two defensible readings will disagree by more than the quantity itself.
0.25 degrees is about 25 km. Hong Kong gets six cells, which is enough to separate water from land but not to resolve the terrain that shapes local ventilation.

Begins 2024-12. Ten months of 2020 (January to October) are also in the download cache from an earlier interrupted run but are NOT in this build; rebuild with --start-year 2020 to include them, noting that their boundary pads are incomplete.
